reason: E2 directly supports that O and N impurities cause nanoscale phase segregation and PFZs in equimolar Ti-V-Nb-Ta, and that this affects mechanical properties, but it does not quantify the strength loss or demonstrate that vacuum processing achieves the claimed 20% strength retention improvement.
premises: Interstitial impurities (O, N) in Ti-V-Nb-Ta promote nanoscale phase segregation during aging at 700 °C
This impurity-induced segregation reduces solid solution strengthening and depletes strength
Impurity depletion near grain boundaries forms precipitate-free zones (PFZs) that degrade properties
Ultra-high vacuum processing can sufficiently reduce O and N to suppress this segregation
Suppressing segregation will retain at least ~20% more yield strength after 700 °C/100 h aging
